chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sa'd ibn Ismail ibn al-Ahwas, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a traveling man to whom death came, so he handed his wealth to a merchant and said, 'This wealth is for so-and-so son of so-and-so. I have neither little nor much in it, so hand it over to him; he may place it wherever he wishes.' The man died and did not give his companion (the one to whom he entrusted it) a specific instruction, nor did his companion know what motivated him to do so. He asked, 'What should he do with it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'He places it wherever he wishes, if he is not commanded otherwise.'

key_terms.يَضَعُهُ: he places it / disposes of it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a trustee when a deceased person leaves wealth with general instructions but no specific command?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the principle of *ikhtiyar* (discretion) in *wakalah* (agency) when the principal dies without issuing a new command. The ruling underscores that unless a specific condition was attached, the trustee retains full authority to distribute the funds as he deems appropriate, reflecting the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in handling ambiguous end-of-life financial trusts. This highlights the importance of clear intent in Islamic inheritance and agency laws, distinguishing between binding directives and discretionary gifts.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Sa’ad Bin Ismail Bin Al Ahows, from his father who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a travelling man to whom death presented itself, so he handed his wealth over to a business man. So he (deceased) said, ‘The wealth is for so and so son of so and so. There is nothing in it for me, little nor more, therefore hand it over to him. He can place it wherever he so desires to’. So the man died and did not order his companion to whom he had made the matter to, nor did he know his companions what is that which he should be carrying upon that. How should he deal with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He places it wherever he so desires to, when there does not happen to be instructions for him’.
en.sarwar: 23. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Sa‘d ibn ’Isma‘ii ibn ai-Ahwas from his father who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man whose death approaches him on a journey. He gives his assets to a man of the merchants saying, ‘This asset belongs to so and so son of so and so. Nothing of it, little or more, belongs to me. You must give it to him, he will place it as he wants’; and he dies, but his friend to whom he has sent the asset does not know anything, there is no instruction and the friend does not know why he has done so. How must he deal with it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He can spend it as he likes when he has not received any instructions.’”
